NER.note: Capacity building of parliamentarians and senior officials is on digital economy issues, not stated as digital-skills training.
No consumer protection rules or redress stated for digital finance.

facts.fact: The coordinator of Niger's Projet Villages Intelligents (PVI), financed by the State and World Bank/IDA, says 3G/4G coverage has reached 657 of 2,175 rural localities in the 8 regions, with a target of 1,400 by end 2025 (the stated date of 31/12/2025 is as given).
facts.system: Projet Villages Intelligents pour la Croissance Rurale et l'Inclusion Numerique (PVI)

facts.fact: The PVI coordinator says the project has trained 350,000 beneficiaries, a majority women, in digital skills through its digital literacy and financial education campaign, with digital centres open in the 8 regions.
facts.system: Projet Villages Intelligents (PVI) digital literacy campaign

NER.note: The project's funding is stated as a joint State and World Bank/IDA total with no state budget line.
No government payments to people stated.
The 16.7% financial inclusion rate (BCEAO, 2022) is not an adult account share from a survey in the window.
Mobile money is named only as a target of the project; no service in use stated.
No tax or fee payment stated.
A fintech challenge prize of March 2022 is stated, with no startup law or public fund.
Digital centres for financial transactions are stated, not tech hubs or incubators.
